findings.reason: a test node building a case that expects kind "redispatch" would either fail against correct code or, worse, be satisfied twice only by the very defect §34 exists to remove, so the clause must name the kind the redispatch path actually records or the path that truly produces "redispatch".
findings.text: §34's done-when asserts "A crew redispatch of a failed plan review in the same home records kind redispatch at attempt 2", but crew redispatch routes through change_lane (reckon/crew/dispatch_sessions.py:1416), which records attempt_kind "lane-change" (dispatch_sessions.py:1741) and lineage kind "lane-change" (:1715), never "redispatch" — so the assertion as written tests an expected value the named verb cannot produce, and the implementer cannot satisfy it by editing the module the section names

findings.reason: the declared scope names a module that cannot host the fix and omits the dispatcher that calls it, so the fence and the write-path estimate for the node are wrong and the worker reaches a path it cannot change without a scope change; the plan already hedges with dispatch.py, but the primary path and the dispatcher belong in the declaration.
findings.text: §34 declares its write path as "the module that composes the plan-review dispatch (reckon/crew/recovery_review_subject.py…)", but that module only composes the node id, brief and argv; the production caller of dispatch() for a composed plan review is recovery_review_dispatch.py:1983, and the attempt/kind decision is computed inside dispatch() from prior committed runs sharing the node id (reckon/crew/dispatch.py:1436-1480) — recovery_review_subject.py cannot set attempt to 1 while §34's own constraint ("the review stores that key on the plan-review-of- prefix are unchanged") forbids changing the node id

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — every cited anchor resolves in the tree at abee30304: reckon/crew/recovery_review_subject.py and reckon/crew/dispatch.py exist, PLAN_REVIEW_NODE_PREFIX is defined (reckon/crew/recovery_vocabulary.py:137, re-exported through recovery.py) and composed into the node id at recovery_review_subject.py:589, PLAN_DERIVED_SCALARS exists (reckon/crew/plan_review.py:133), the §5 fixtures (legacy_plan.html, current_plan.html, derived_impl_plan.html) and the §6/§24 test files exist, and the run directory cited carries attempt-34-worker.json and attempt-34-exit.json.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §34's done-when is measurable and carries a negative control, but its second clause names an expected `attempt_kind` that the verb it names does not produce.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — every gate is a committed test under tests/ (tests/test_a_new_plan_review_is_a_first_attempt.py, tests/test_bookkeeping_earns_no_review.py) and the declared control log sits under the run directory on the crew home, which survives the run, not a session scratchpad or node-local temp path.
rubric_items.naming: pass — §34's names (attempt, attempt_kind, dispatch, redispatch) are mechanism terms, and the new test file is named for what it asserts rather than for any plan label, stage or ticket.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §34's stated root cause is confirmed against the code and the cited run artifacts (reckon/crew/dispatch.py:1436-1480 computes attempt/kind from prior committed runs sharing the node id; the review node id is one per plan; attempt-34-worker.json corroborates it) and both named readers of the misread number exist (reckon/calibration.py:126, reckon/crew/picker/types.py:17), but the mechanism's caller is misnamed, so the fix cannot be made where the plan points first.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §34 names one deliverable (a fresh composed review dispatches as attempt 1 with kind dispatch, while a genuine redispatch still records its own kind), and §24's deferred measure is likewise a single goal.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — the plan's only relationship declaration is plan-informs (an-orchestrator-is-bound-by-its-inbox, the-local-lane-is-the-default), both of which resolve to existing plans under docs/plans/, and the one implementable section (§34) needs no missing dependency or gate.
